concepts.name: Governor: appointment, qualifications, conditions, immunities and term
concepts.description: How a Governor is appointed, who qualifies, the conditions of office, oath, Article 361 immunities, term, removal and Article 160.
concepts.idea: The Governor is a nominee of the President in a constitutional office with two qualifications, a five-year term at the President's pleasure and limited personal immunities.
concepts.rule: Articles 153 to 167 deal with the State Executive. The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant (Article 155), the Canadian model being preferred to an elected Governor, and must be a citizen of 35 years (Article 157). He holds no other office of profit, cannot sit in a legislature, and his emoluments cannot be reduced (Article 158). He takes an oath before the High Court Chief Justice (Article 159), enjoys immunity from criminal proceedings during his term and civil proceedings for personal acts only after two months' notice, serves five years at the President's pleasure and continues until a successor takes charge. Article 160 lets the President provide for contingencies.
concepts.example: A sitting Governor dies; the President may ask the High Court Chief Justice to act.

questions.q: Two neighbouring States are, for the time being, served by one and the same person as Governor. Which constitutional provision made such an arrangement possible?
questions.a: The proviso to Article 153, inserted by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956, for a joint Governor
o: The proviso to Article 153, inserted by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956, for a joint Governor
Article 156, which fixes the Governor's term of office and makes it subject to the President's pleasure
Article 157, which prescribes the qualifications for appointment as Governor of a State
Article 155, which provides that the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal
questions.e: Article 153 says there shall be a Governor for each State; its proviso, added by the 7th Amendment Act 1956, allows the same person to be Governor of two or more States.
w: Article 156 deals with the Governor's term and pleasure; it does not allow one person to serve two States.
Article 157 prescribes only the qualifications (citizen, 35 years); it has no provision on a joint Governor.
Article 155 deals with the mode of appointment; the enabling proviso is in Article 153.

questions.q: Article 157 of the Constitution prescribes who can be appointed as a Governor. Which one of the following correctly states what it requires?
questions.a: Citizenship of India and completion of 35 years of age, with no other qualification prescribed
o: Citizenship of India and completion of 35 years of age, with no other qualification prescribed
Citizenship of India, completion of 35 years and a degree from a recognised university
Citizenship of India, completion of 30 years and enrolment as a voter in the State concerned
Citizenship of India, completion of 35 years and previous membership of Parliament or a State Legislature
questions.e: Article 157 lays down only two qualifications: Indian citizenship and 35 completed years. No educational, professional or political qualification is specified.
w: No educational qualification is prescribed for a Governor.
The minimum age is 35, not 30, and residence or enrolment in the State is not a requirement.
No political experience is prescribed; indeed a sitting legislator must give up the seat on becoming Governor.

questions.q: A newly appointed Governor is to be sworn in on a day when the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State is unavailable. Before whom may the oath or affirmation be made?
questions.a: The senior-most Judge of that High Court who is available
o: The senior-most Judge of that High Court who is available
The senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court who is present in the State capital
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of the State
The Chief Minister of the State, as the head of the Council of Ministers
questions.e: Under Article 159 the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge of that Court available.
w: The oath is administered within the High Court of the State, not by a Supreme Court Judge.
A legislative presiding officer has no role in administering the Governor's oath.
The Chief Minister is advised by, and is subordinate in form to, the Governor and does not swear him in.

questions.q: Which one of the following describes the model which the Constituent Assembly accepted for choosing State Governors?
questions.a: A Canadian-type arrangement, with the head of the province appointed from the centre by the federal government
o: A Canadian-type arrangement, with the head of the province appointed from the centre by the federal government
An American-type arrangement, in which the head of the State is elected directly by the voters of the State
An indirect-election arrangement, in which an electoral college of both Houses of the State Legislature elects the Governor
A legislature-choice arrangement, in which the State Legislature itself selects the head of the State
questions.e: The Governor is appointed by the President and not elected; the framers followed the Canadian model, where provincial heads are appointed from the centre, rather than the American model of an elected Governor.
w: This was the direct-election model of the Draft Constitution, which the Assembly dropped.
No electoral college is used; the Governor is neither directly nor indirectly elected.
The Governor is not chosen by the State Legislature; the President alone appoints him.

questions.q: The death of a sitting Governor leaves the office without anyone to discharge its functions. Which of the following is the constitutional route for such a situation?
questions.a: The President may make provision under Article 160, such as asking the High Court Chief Justice to act temporarily
o: The President may make provision under Article 160, such as asking the High Court Chief Justice to act temporarily
A Vice-Governor, appointed together with every Governor, takes over automatically under Article 153 on his death
The Chief Minister becomes the acting Governor by virtue of the aid and advice clause in Article 163 until a successor arrives
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly acts as Governor until a successor is appointed under Article 164, as senior elected officer
questions.e: Article 160 lets the President make provision for the discharge of the Governor's functions in any contingency the Constitution does not cover; a standard example is the death of a sitting Governor, with the High Court Chief Justice acting temporarily.
w: There is no office of Vice-Governor in a State, unlike the Vice-President at the Centre.
Article 163 deals with ministerial advice; it does not make the Chief Minister a Governor.
Article 164 deals with Ministers; the Speaker has no such constitutional role.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of a Governor:

1. The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
2. The Governor is indirectly elected through an electoral college resembling the one for the President.
3. The Sarkaria Commission recommended that a person from outside the State be appointed as Governor.
4. Article 155 obliges the President to consult the Chief Minister of the State before appointing the Governor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 155 provides this. Statement 2 is incorrect: He is neither directly nor indirectly elected and no electoral college is involved. Statement 3 is correct: It listed 'a person from outside the state' among its criteria. Statement 4 is incorrect: Consultation is only desirable by convention; the Sarkaria Commission wanted it written into Article 155, which has not been done.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the conditions of the Governor's office laid down in Article 158:

1. A member of a State Legislature who is appointed Governor is deemed to have vacated the seat on the date he enters office.
2. The Governor may hold another office of profit during his first year in office.
3. An Act of Parliament may reduce the emoluments and allowances of a Governor during his term of office.
4. If one person is Governor of two or more States, the President decides by order the proportion in which the States share his emoluments.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The same applies to a member of either House of Parliament. Statement 2 is incorrect: He cannot hold any other office of profit. Statement 3 is incorrect: His emoluments and allowances cannot be diminished during his term. Statement 4 is correct: This is stated in the conditions of office.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the immunities of a Governor under Article 361:

1. For acts done in his official capacity, the Governor is personally immune from legal liability.
2. While he is in office, no criminal proceeding can be started or continued against him even for his personal acts.
3. Civil proceedings for his personal acts can be instituted during his term after one month's notice.
4. The Governor's immunity for acts done in the exercise of his official powers does not lapse when he ceases to hold office.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 361 the Governor is personally immune from legal liability for acts done in his official capacity; the immunity protects the office. Statement 2 is correct: while he is in office no criminal proceeding can be started or continued against him even for personal acts, and he cannot be arrested or imprisoned. Statement 3 is incorrect: the notice period is two months, and it must state the nature of the proceedings and the cause of action. Statement 4 is correct: Article 361(1) shields the Governor from answerability for the exercise of his official powers and duties, and that protection is not confined to the term of office.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the term and removal of a Governor:

1. A Governor holds office for a term of six years from the date on which he enters upon the office, subject to the pleasure of the President.
2. The Constitution prescribes grounds and an impeachment-type procedure for removing a Governor.
3. Under the doctrine of pleasure the President may remove a Governor at any time, and need not disclose his reasons for doing so.
4. A Governor must vacate office on the day his five-year term ends, even if no successor has assumed charge.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The term is five years, subject to the pleasure of the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: No grounds or procedure are prescribed and no inquiry is needed. Statement 3 is correct: The Governor has no independent security of tenure, and no ground for removal is prescribed, so the President need not disclose reasons. Statement 4 is incorrect: He continues until his successor assumes charge so that the office is never vacant.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the oath or affirmation of a Governor under Article 159:

1. The Governor makes and subscribes the oath or affirmation before entering upon his office.
2. In his oath the Governor undertakes to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.
3. The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the State High Court or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge available.
4. A person discharging the functions of the Governor, including an Acting Governor, takes the same oath or affirmation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 159 requires the oath or affirmation before entering upon office. Statement 2 is incorrect: that wording (true faith and allegiance, upholding sovereignty and integrity) belongs to the oath of Ministers; the Governor swears to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law. Statement 3 is correct: Article 159 provides that the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court or, in his absence, the senior-most Judge available. Statement 4 is correct: Article 159 applies the same oath to any person discharging the functions of the Governor.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor and the executive power of the State:

1. Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Chief Minister, who exercises it through the Council of Ministers.
2. Article 163 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor, except where he must act in his discretion.
3. Article 164 makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly.
4. After the 42nd Amendment of 1976, ministerial advice is binding on the Governor just as it is on the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor, exercisable directly or through officers subordinate to him; it is not vested in the Chief Minister. Statement 2 is correct: Article 163 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor, except where he must act in his discretion. Statement 3 is correct: This is the foundation of the parliamentary system in the State. Statement 4 is incorrect: The 42nd Amendment made advice binding on the President only; no such provision exists for the Governor.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the office of Governor:

1. In the Hargovind Pant case (1979) the Supreme Court held that the Governor's office is an employment under the Central government.
2. In the Surya Narain case (1981) the Rajasthan High Court held that the pleasure of the President is not justiciable.
3. The President may transfer a Governor appointed to one State to another State for the rest of the term, and a Governor whose term has expired may be reappointed.
4. In 2018 Parliament raised the Governor's salary from Rs 1.10 lakh to Rs 3.50 lakh per month.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: in Hargovind Pant (1979) the Supreme Court held that the Governor's office is an independent constitutional office, not under the Centre's control. Statement 2 is correct: in Surya Narain (1981) it was held that the pleasure of the President is not justiciable, so removal needs no stated grounds. Statement 3 is correct: the President may transfer a Governor appointed to one State to another State for the rest of the term, and a Governor whose term has expired may be reappointed. Statement 4 is correct: the Finance Act 2018 raised the salary from Rs 1.10 lakh to Rs 3.50 lakh per month.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the rejection of an elected Governor in the Constituent Assembly:

1. Direct election was considered incompatible with the parliamentary system set up in the States.
2. An elected Governor would belong to a party and might not be a neutral, impartial head.
3. Presidential nomination was seen as enabling the Centre to keep its control over the States.
4. The Canadian model, in which the provincial head is appointed from the centre, was preferred to the American model of an elected Governor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: direct election of the Governor was considered incompatible with the parliamentary system set up in the States. Statement 2 is correct: an elected Governor would belong to a party and might not be a neutral, impartial head. Statement 3 is correct: nomination by the President was seen as enabling the Centre to keep its control over the States. Statement 4 is correct: the Constituent Assembly preferred the Canadian model of a centrally appointed provincial head to the American model of an elected Governor.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Executive and the Governor:

1. Part VI, comprising Articles 152 to 237, deals with the governance of the Union Territories.
2. Articles 153 to 167 specifically relate to the State Executive.
3. Like the Vice-President at the Centre, there is a Vice-Governor in each State to take over when the Governor is absent.
4. The Constitution envisages the possibility of the Governor acting in his discretion, but no such possibility for the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Part VI deals with the States listed in the First Schedule, not the Union Territories. Statement 2 is correct: Articles 153 to 167 specifically relate to the State Executive. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is no office of Vice-Governor in a State. Statement 4 is correct: under Article 163 the Constitution envisages the Governor acting in his discretion, but makes no such provision for the President.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's emoluments and residence:

1. The Governor holds no other office of profit while in office.
2. The Governor is entitled to use an official residence free of rent.
3. The emoluments, allowances and privileges of the Governor are fixed by the State Legislature.
4. Until Parliament makes such a law, the Third Schedule governs his emoluments.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Governor holds no other office of profit while in office. Statement 2 is correct: he is entitled to use his official residence, the Raj Bhavan, without payment of rent. Statement 3 is incorrect: his emoluments, allowances and privileges are fixed by Parliament by law. Statement 4 is incorrect: until then the Second Schedule, not the Third, governs. So exactly 2 statements are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct (1 and 2).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct (1 and 2).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct (1 and 2).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 160 and the functions of a Governor in a contingency:

1. Article 160 lets the President provide for discharge of the Governor's functions in a contingency the Constitution does not cover.
2. Article 160 can be invoked only on the death of a sitting Governor.
3. A person who discharges the functions of the Governor under such a provision is exempt from taking the oath.
4. In the absence of the Governor, the Vice-Governor of the State discharges his functions.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 160 lets the President provide for discharge of the Governor's functions in a contingency the Constitution does not cover. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 160 is not confined to a vacancy; it also covers absence, inability or any other exceptional situation affecting the office. Statement 3 is incorrect: Any person discharging the Governor's functions takes the same oath or affirmation. Statement 4 is incorrect: There is no office of Vice-Governor in a State. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the resignation, transfer and reappointment of a Governor:

1. A Governor may resign at any time by a written resignation addressed to the President.
2. The President may transfer a Governor from one State to another.
3. A Governor whose term has expired may be reappointed in the same State or in another State.
4. A Governor's resignation is addressed to the Chief Minister of the State.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A Governor may resign at any time by a written resignation addressed to the President. Statement 2 is correct: The President may transfer a Governor from one State to another. Statement 3 is correct: A Governor whose term has expired may be reappointed in the same State or in another State. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is addressed to the President, who appointed him. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Criminal proceedings for his personal acts can be started against a person who has ceased to be Governor.
Statement-II: The Governor's immunity from criminal proceedings, even for personal acts, operates only during his term of office.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Criminal immunity for personal acts is temporary; proceedings can be started or continued after the Governor leaves office. Statement-II is correct: During his term of office the Governor is immune from any criminal proceedings, even for personal acts. Because the bar operates only during the term, nothing prevents proceedings once he ceases to be Governor, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II is the reason behind Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The emoluments and allowances of a Governor cannot be reduced during his term of office.
Statement-II: The emoluments of a Governor are fixed by the State Legislature and are therefore beyond Parliament's reach.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: : the emoluments cannot be diminished during the term. Statement-II is incorrect: : emoluments, allowances and privileges are fixed by Parliament by law, not by the State Legislature. Statement-II is wrong because they are fixed by Parliament by law, so it cannot be the reason.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is incorrect, so "both correct" fails.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the Articles on the Governor in List-I with what each deals with in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 155
B. Article 157
C. Article 158
D. Article 160

List-II
1. Conditions of the Governor's office
2. Appointment of the Governor
3. Discharge of the Governor's functions in certain contingencies
4. Qualifications for appointment as Governor
questions.e: Article 155 is the appointment of the Governor, Article 157 the qualifications, Article 158 the conditions of office and Article 160 the contingency provision.
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 155 is about appointment and Article 157 about qualifications.
C and D are interchanged: Article 158 gives the conditions and Article 160 the contingency provision.
A and C are interchanged: Article 155 is not the conditions and Article 158 is not the appointment.

concepts.name: Governor: executive, legislative, financial and judicial powers
concepts.description: The four heads of the Governor's powers, ordinances and the process of Articles 200 and 201.
concepts.idea: The Governor has executive, legislative, financial and judicial powers like the President but no diplomatic, military or emergency powers.
concepts.rule: Executive action is taken in his name; he appoints the Chief Minister and, on the Chief Minister's advice, Ministers, and the Advocate-General, State Election Commissioner and SPSC members. He summons and prorogues the Legislature, dissolves the Assembly, nominates one-sixth of the Council, promulgates ordinances (six weeks from reassembly) and assents to, withholds assent from, returns or reserves Bills. Money Bills need his recommendation; he makes advances from the Contingency Fund and constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years. He may suspend, remit or commute but not pardon a death sentence and has no clemency power in court-martial cases.
concepts.example: A re-passed Bill must receive assent; a Money Bill cannot be returned.

questions.q: In which one of the following sets are all the powers ones that the President of India enjoys but a Governor does not?
questions.a: Diplomatic, military and emergency powers, none of which a Governor has
o: Diplomatic, military and emergency powers, none of which a Governor has
Executive powers, financial powers and ordinance-making powers
Pardoning powers, legislative powers and powers over the Budget
Powers of appointing Ministers, judicial officers and the Advocate-General
questions.e: A Governor has executive, legislative, financial and judicial powers more or less analogous to the President's, but no diplomatic, military or emergency powers.
w: A Governor has executive and financial powers and can promulgate ordinances.
A Governor can grant clemency for State-law offences, summon the Legislature and see that the Budget is laid before it.
The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, Ministers, district judges and the Advocate-General.

questions.q: Unforeseen expenditure of a State, before the Legislature has authorised it, is met by the Governor through advances out of which fund?
questions.a: The Contingency Fund of the State, with the expenditure later regularised by the Legislature
o: The Contingency Fund of the State, with the expenditure later regularised by the Legislature
The Consolidated Fund of the State, with the expenditure later regularised by the Legislature
The Public Account of the State, with the expenditure later regularised by the Legislature
The Contingency Fund of India, with the expenditure later regularised by Parliament
questions.e: The Governor makes advances out of the State Contingency Fund for unforeseen expenditure, which is later regularised by the Legislature through appropriation.
w: Money from the Consolidated Fund can be spent only after appropriation; the advance is made from the Contingency Fund.
The Public Account holds funds the State receives as banker; it is not the source for unforeseen advances.
That fund is operated by the President for Union expenditure, not by the Governor.

questions.q: A person convicted under a law within the executive power of a State has been sentenced to death. Which one of the following is the extent of the Governor's clemency power over that sentence?
questions.a: He can suspend, remit or commute the sentence but cannot pardon it
o: He can suspend, remit or commute the sentence but cannot pardon it
He can pardon the sentence, since the offence is against a State law
He has no power at all over the sentence, which lies exclusively with the President
He can pardon it only after the State High Court recommends it
questions.e: Under Article 161 the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence even if a State law prescribes it (the power to pardon a death sentence is the President's under Article 72), but he can suspend, remit or commute it; he acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
w: Even where a State law prescribes death, the power to pardon the death sentence lies with the President.
The Governor can suspend, remit or commute a death sentence; only the pardon is reserved to the President.
No High Court recommendation can enlarge his power; he cannot pardon a death sentence.

questions.q: A vacancy has to be filled in the State judicial service in a post below that of District Judge. Whom must the Governor consult before making the appointment?
questions.a: The High Court of the State and the State Public Service Commission
o: The High Court of the State and the State Public Service Commission
The State High Court, without any reference to the State Public Service Commission
The State Public Service Commission and the Advocate-General of the State
The Chief Justice of India and the Law Commission of the State
questions.e: The Governor appoints persons to the State judicial service other than district judges in consultation with the High Court and the State Public Service Commission; district judges are appointed in consultation with the High Court.
w: The Governor must consult the State Public Service Commission as well.
The Advocate-General has no role; the High Court must be consulted.
Neither is consulted for State judicial service appointments.

questions.q: An ordinance promulgated by a Governor, must be approved by the State Legislature within what period?
questions.a: Six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature
o: Six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature
Four weeks from the date of promulgation
Six months from the date of promulgation
Three months from the reassembly of the Legislature
questions.e: A Governor's ordinance is to be laid before the Legislature and ceases to operate six weeks after reassembly, or earlier if disapproved.
w: The period runs from reassembly of the Legislature, and it is six weeks.
Six months is not the period for approval of a Governor's ordinance.
Three months is not the period; the ordinance ceases after six weeks from reassembly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the executive powers of the Governor:

1. All executive action of the State Government is formally taken in the Governor's name, and an authenticated order cannot be questioned for not being made by the Governor personally.
2. The Governor frames rules for the convenient transaction of State business and for allocation of business among Ministers, in practice on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
3. The 94th Amendment Act, 2006 made it mandatory to have a Tribal Welfare Minister in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.
4. The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and other Ministers are appointed by him on the Chief Minister's advice and hold office during his pleasure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 166 all executive action of the State Government is formally taken in the Governor's name, and an authenticated order cannot be questioned for not being made by him personally. Statement 2 is correct: the Governor frames rules for the convenient transaction of State business and for allocation of business among Ministers, in practice on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 94th Amendment Act freed Bihar from the requirement and extended it to Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, so the four States are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. concepts.name: Bills, reservation, Article 356 and the hung Assembly
concepts.description: Governor versus President on Bills, types of veto, categories of reservation, Article 356, Bommai and the Sarkaria order.
concepts.idea: The Governor's Bill powers add reservation to the President's three options, and his discretion in a hung House is guided by floor tests and the Sarkaria order.
concepts.rule: On ordinary Bills both have a suspensive veto, but only the Governor can reserve. A reserved Money Bill can only be assented to or withheld by the President. Reservation is compulsory for Bills endangering the High Court and arises under provisions such as Articles 360, 31A, 31C, 254(2), 288(2) and 304(b). In Article 356 the Governor reports and the President decides; Bommai made it justiciable. In a hung House the Sarkaria order is: pre-poll alliance, largest single party, post-poll coalition with all joining, post-poll alliance with outside support, with a floor test.
concepts.example: A Bill derogating from High Court powers must be reserved.

concepts.name: Chief Minister: position, dismissal and powers
concepts.description: The Chief Minister's tenure, dependence on the Assembly's confidence, judicial rulings on dismissal, and powers over Ministers, the Governor and the legislature.
concepts.idea: The Chief Minister is the real executive whose tenure rests on the Assembly's confidence rather than the Governor's pleasure.
concepts.rule: The Governor is the de jure head and the Chief Minister the de facto head, like the Prime Minister. A Chief Minister with a majority cannot be dismissed, majority is tested on the floor (Bommai, Jagdambika Pal), and advice to dissolve is normally binding. The Chief Minister recommends Ministers, allocates portfolios, can ask a Minister to resign, presides over the Cabinet and his resignation ends the Council. He chairs the State Planning Board, is vice-chairman of a Zonal Council by rotation and a member of the Inter-State Council and NITI Aayog Governing Council.
concepts.example: Jagdambika Pal led to a composite floor test.

questions.q: In a State, the Chief Minister resigns. Which one of the following is the constitutional consequence for the Council of Ministers, in contrast with the resignation of some other Minister?

questions.e: The Chief Minister is the head of the Council; his resignation or death automatically dissolves it, while the resignation of another Minister only creates a vacancy that the Chief Minister may or may not fill.
w: The Council exists only as long as the Chief Minister does; there is no automatic successor by seniority.
The resignation of the Chief Minister dissolves the entire Council, not merely the Cabinet.
Resignation of the Chief Minister does not dissolve the Assembly.

Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: in practice the Governor can appoint to the Council of Ministers only those whom the Chief Minister recommends. The constitutional requirement of the Chief Minister's advice is the reason the Governor has no independent say, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: The Chief Minister is the political head of the services and influences them through transfers and postings within legal limits. Statement-II is correct. questions.e: The Chief Minister chairs the State Planning Board, is vice-chairman of the Zonal Council by rotation for a year, is a member of the Inter-State Council under the Prime Minister, and Article 167 imposes the duty of furnishing information.

concepts.name: State Council of Ministers: Articles 163, 164, 166, 167 and 177
concepts.description: Constitutional provisions on the Council, size limits, tribal welfare Minister, oath, non-members and the nature of ministerial advice.
concepts.idea: Articles 163 and 164 make the Council the aid and advice body of the Governor, with size limits, the six-month rule and limited judicial inquiry.
concepts.rule: Article 163 provides a Council headed by the Chief Minister; the Governor decides what is discretion and courts cannot inquire into advice. Article 164 (as amended by the 91st Amendment, 2003) caps the Council at 15 per cent of the Assembly with a minimum of 12 and bars defectors; Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha must have a tribal welfare Minister (94th Amendment). A non-member may be Minister for six consecutive months only. Article 166 puts action in the Governor's name, Article 167 binds the Chief Minister to inform the Governor, and Article 177 lets Ministers speak but not vote. B.R. Kapur barred a disqualified person.
concepts.example: A convicted person cannot be made Chief Minister even temporarily.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly states the limit on the size of a State Council of Ministers and the amendment that introduced it?
questions.a: No more than 15 per cent of the Assembly's strength and no fewer than 12 including the Chief Minister, by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003
o: No more than 15 per cent of the Assembly's strength and no fewer than 12 including the Chief Minister, by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003
Not more than 10 per cent of the Assembly's strength and not fewer than 12 including the Chief Minister, by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003
Not more than 15 per cent of the Assembly's strength and not fewer than 10, by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003
Not more than 15 per cent of the Assembly's strength and not fewer than 12 including the Chief Minister, by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act 2003 inserted Article 164(1A): ministers, including the Chief Minister, not more than 15 per cent of the Assembly strength and not fewer than 12.
w: The ceiling is 15 per cent, not 10 per cent.
The floor is 12, not 10.
The limits were inserted by the 91st Amendment in 2003; the 42nd Amendment did not do this.

questions.q: Under Article 164 as amended by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006, which of the following sets of States must have a Minister in charge of tribal welfare?
questions.a: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
o: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Maharashtra
questions.e: The four States are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; Bihar was excluded because it has no Scheduled Areas now and very few Scheduled Tribes.
w: Bihar was freed from the obligation by the 94th Amendment.
Maharashtra is not required to have a tribal welfare Minister under Article 164.
Madhya Pradesh is among the States; Maharashtra is not.

questions.q: A member of a State Legislature has been disqualified on the ground of defection. For how long is he disqualified from being appointed a Minister?
questions.a: For the rest of the Legislature's term, or until he is elected afresh if that happens earlier, under Article 164
o: For the rest of the Legislature's term, or until he is elected afresh if that happens earlier, under Article 164
For a period of six years from the date of disqualification, whatever the remaining term of the Legislature
For the remainder of his life, since disqualification on the ground of defection operates as a permanent bar to office
Until the next general election to the Lok Sabha is held, even if the State Legislature's term has not ended
questions.e: Article 164(1B), inserted by the 91st Amendment, bars him for the rest of the term or until his next election, whichever is earlier.
w: The period is tied to the Legislature's term or re-election, not to a fixed six years.
The bar is temporary and is not lifelong.
The next election to the Lok Sabha has no bearing on the bar.

questions.q: A person is a member of the Legislative Council only. What is the position of that person, as a Minister, in the Legislative Assembly of the State?
questions.a: He may speak and take part in its proceedings but cannot vote there
o: He may speak and take part in its proceedings but cannot vote there
He may speak and vote there, as a Minister of the State
He may take part in its proceedings and vote, but only on matters concerning his own portfolio
He may speak only with the Speaker's special permission and cannot take part in debates
questions.e: Under Article 177 every Minister may speak and take part in the proceedings of the Assembly (and the Council) but cannot vote unless he is a member of that House.
w: Being a member of the other House, he cannot vote in the Assembly.
Article 177 gives him no vote in a House of which he is not a member, even on his own portfolio.
Article 177 gives him a right to speak and take part in its proceedings.

questions.q: Who decides whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion, and can an act of his be questioned on the ground that he ought not to have acted in his discretion?
questions.a: The Governor himself decides, and the act cannot be questioned on the ground that he ought not to have used discretion
o: The Governor himself decides, and the act cannot be questioned on the ground that he ought not to have used discretion
The Advocate-General decides on a reference by the Governor, and the matter can be taken to the High Court for review
The Chief Minister decides on behalf of the Council, and the Assembly can question the act by a resolution
The High Court decides on a reference from the Governor, and the act can be questioned there on that ground
questions.e: Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on whether a matter is discretionary final; validity of his act cannot be questioned on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in discretion; finality does not allow arbitrariness.
w: The decision rests with the Governor, not with the Advocate-General.
The Chief Minister has no role in deciding whether a matter is in the Governor's discretion.
Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision final; no reference to the High Court is required.

questions.q:

3. Under Article 163(3) the courts cannot inquire into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor.
4. The State Council of Ministers resembles the Union Council of Ministers, and its essential parliamentary features lie in Articles 163 and 164.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 163(1) provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor, except where the Constitution requires him to act in his discretion. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Governor's decision on this is final. Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 163(3) the courts cannot inquire into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor. Statement 4 is correct: The State Council of Ministers resembles the Union Council of Ministers, and its essential parliamentary features lie in Articles 163 and 164.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment and tenure of Ministers under Article 164:

1. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, and the other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
2. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, but this pleasure is conditioned by majority support in the Assembly.
3. In S.R. Bommai (1994) the Supreme Court held that a ministry with majority support can be dismissed by the Governor at his pleasure.
4. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Council of the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, and the other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister. Statement 2 is correct: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, but this pleasure is conditioned by majority support in the Assembly. Statement 3 is incorrect: Bommai is cited for the point that a ministry with majority support cannot be dismissed arbitrarily. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ministers of a State:

1. The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, must not exceed 15 per cent of the strength of the Legislative Assembly and must not be fewer than 12.
2. The Governor can remove an individual Minister on his own initiative, without the advice of the Chief Minister.
3. Wherever the Constitution requires the satisfaction of the Governor, it is the satisfaction of the Council of Ministers and not his personal satisfaction.
4. A Minister who is not a member of the Legislature for twelve consecutive months ceases to be a Minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, must not exceed 15 per cent of the strength of the Legislative Assembly and must not be fewer than 12. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Governor can remove a Minister only on the advice of the Chief Minister. Statement 3 is correct: Shamsher Singh (1974). Statement 4 is incorrect: The period is six consecutive months.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the provisions inserted in Article 164:

1. The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Clauses (1A) and (1B) in Article 164.
2. Article 164(1A) fixes the ceiling of 15 per cent and a floor of 12 for the number of Ministers in a State.
3. A member disqualified on the ground of defection cannot be appointed a Minister for the rest of the Legislature's term or until his next election, whichever is earlier.
4. The Tribal Welfare Minister may also be put in charge of the welfare of Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes or other work decided by the State Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It was the 91st Amendment Act, 2003. Statement 2 is correct: Article 164(1A) fixes the ceiling of 15 per cent and a floor of 12 for the number of Ministers in a State. Statement 3 is correct: A member disqualified on the ground of defection cannot be appointed a Minister for the rest of the Legislature's term or until his next election, whichever is earlier. Statement 4 is correct: The Tribal Welfare Minister may also be put in charge of the welfare of Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes or other work decided by the State Government.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the oaths and salaries of Ministers:

1. The Governor administers the oath of office to Ministers under Article 164(3).
2. A Minister's oath of office includes a pledge to do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law, without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.
3. The oath of secrecy binds the Minister not to disclose confidential matters except as needed for official duty.
4. The form of the oaths of office and secrecy for Ministers is prescribed in the Second Schedule.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Governor administers the oath of office to Ministers under Article 164(3). Statement 2 is correct: A Minister's oath of office includes a pledge to do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law, without fear or favour, affection or ill-will. Statement 3 is correct: The oath of secrecy binds the Minister not to disclose confidential matters except as needed for official duty. Statement 4 is incorrect: The forms are in the Third Schedule; the Second Schedule deals with emoluments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 166, 167 and 177:

1. Under Article 166 all executive action of the State is taken in the name of the Governor, and orders must be authenticated as the Governor specifies.
2. The Rules of Business governing the allocation of work among Ministers are framed by the State Legislature.
3. Article 167 requires the Governor to communicate to the Chief Minister all his decisions on administration and legislation.
4. Under Article 177 a Minister who is not a member of a House can vote in that House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 166 all executive action of the State is taken in the name of the Governor, and orders must be authenticated as the Governor specifies. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Governor frames them, though real decisions are taken by the Council of Ministers. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 167 places the duty on the Chief Minister to communicate Council decisions to the Governor. 4. Article 164(4) bars a Member of Parliament who is not a member of the State Legislature from being appointed a State Minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A person who is not a member of the State Legislature may be appointed Chief Minister or Minister. Statement 2 is correct: The six-month limit in Article 164(4) is mandatory and the Minister ceases to hold office when the period expires without his becoming a member. Statement 3 is correct: the Supreme Court reasoned from responsible-government practice (S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab, 2001). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 164(4) does not bar such a person, subject to the six-month rule.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about B.R. Kapur v. State of Tamil Nadu and the limits on appointing a non-legislator:

1. The appointee need only be a citizen of India; qualifications for membership of the Legislature are not relevant to the Governor's power.
2. The Supreme Court quashed the appointment of Jayalalithaa as Chief Minister because she had been convicted and was disqualified from legislature membership.
3. A person disqualified from contesting elections cannot be made Chief Minister even temporarily, as what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly through Article 164(4).
4. Popular support for the leader of the majority party can override a constitutional disqualification.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The appointee must meet the qualifications for Legislature membership and have no disqualification on the date of appointment. Statement 2 is correct: The Supreme Court quashed the appointment of Jayalalithaa as Chief Minister because she had been convicted and was disqualified from legislature membership. Statement 3 is correct: A person disqualified from contesting elections cannot be made Chief Minister even temporarily, as what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly through Article 164(4). questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the advice of the Council of Ministers and the Governor:

1. The advice of the Council under Article 163 is collective and binding on the Governor in all non-discretionary matters, mirroring Article 74 at the Union level.
2. In Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab (1974) the Supreme Court said the Governor has very limited discretionary powers, to be strictly construed.
3. There must always be a Council of Ministers to advise the Governor; after dissolution of the Assembly or resignation of the Council the outgoing ministry continues as caretaker until a new ministry is appointed.
4. In Nabam Rebia (2016) the Supreme Court reaffirmed that outside discretionary matters the Governor acts only on aid and advice.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The advice of the Council under Article 163 is collective and binding on the Governor in all non-discretionary matters, mirroring Article 74 at the Union level. Statement 2 is correct: In Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab (1974) the Supreme Court said the Governor has very limited discretionary powers, to be strictly construed. Statement 3 is correct: There must always be a Council of Ministers to advise the Governor; after dissolution of the Assembly or resignation of the Council the outgoing ministry continues as caretaker until a new ministry is appointed. Statement 4 is correct: In Nabam Rebia (2016) the Supreme Court reaffirmed that outside discretionary matters the Governor acts only on aid and advice.

'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial inquiry and the Governor's discretion:

1. Article 163(3) bars judicial inquiry into whether Ministers advised the Governor and what the advice was, so courts cannot summon records of such advice.
2. In U.N.R. Rao v. Indira Gandhi (1971) the Supreme Court held that Article 74 is mandatory and the President cannot exercise executive power without the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, and that the Council of Ministers does not cease to hold office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
3. The Governor's discretion may flow from his personal wisdom where the Constitution is silent.
4. The outgoing ministry ceases to exist the moment the Assembly is dissolved, leaving the Governor to act alone until a new ministry is appointed.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 163(3) bars judicial inquiry into whether Ministers advised the Governor and what the advice was, so courts cannot summon records of such advice. Statement 2 is correct: In U.N.R. Rao v. Indira Gandhi (1971) the Supreme Court held that Article 74 is mandatory, so the President cannot exercise executive power without the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, and that the Council does not cease to hold office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is incorrect: It must flow from constitutional text, conventions or judicially recognised situations, not personal wisdom. Statement 4 is incorrect: The outgoing ministry continues as caretaker until a new ministry is appointed. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

3. A Minister gets the salary and allowances payable to a member of the State Legislature plus a sumptuary allowance according to rank, free accommodation and travelling allowance.
4. The Governor fixes the salaries and allowances of Ministers by rules.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The salaries and allowances of Ministers are determined by the State Legislature by law. Statement 2 is correct: Until the Legislature does so, they are as specified in the Second Schedule. Statement 3 is correct: a Minister gets the salary and allowances payable to a member of the State Legislature plus a sumptuary allowance according to rank, free accommodation and travelling allowance. Statement 4 is incorrect: The State Legislature decides them by law. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

Consider the following statements about Article 164:

1. Article 164(1A) fixes the ceiling and the floor on the size of the ministry.
2. The Tribal Welfare Minister in a State covered by the proviso to Article 164(1) cannot be given charge of any other subject.

4. A Minister who is not a member of the Legislature may continue for twelve months before he must resign.

Statement 2 is incorrect: He may also be put in charge of the welfare of Scheduled Castes and backward classes or other work. Statement 3 is incorrect: Bihar was excluded by the 94th Amendment. Statement 4 is incorrect: The limit is six consecutive months. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect

questions.q:
Match the Articles of Part VI dealing with Ministers in List-I with their subject in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 163
B. Article 166
C. Article 167
D. Article 177

List-II
1. Conduct of business of the Government of a State
2. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor
3. Duties of the Chief Minister as respects furnishing of information to the Governor
4. Rights of Ministers as respects the Houses
questions.e: Article 163 provides for the Council to aid and advise; 166 for conduct of business; 167 for the Chief Minister's duty of information; 177 for rights of Ministers in the Houses.

concepts.name: Ministers, Cabinet, Cabinet Committees and the Advocate-General
concepts.description: Categories of Ministers, the Cabinet and its committees, the Advocate-General and a comparison with the Attorney General.
concepts.idea: The Council has conventional ranks and a convention-based Cabinet, while the Advocate-General is the Governor's appointed chief law officer of the State.
concepts.rule: The Chief Minister fixes the Council's size and ranks: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers by convention; the Deputy Chief Minister is not in the Constitution. The Cabinet is the highest policy body and Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional. The Advocate-General (Article 165) is appointed by the Governor, must be qualified for a High Court Judge, holds office at the Governor's pleasure, can speak in the legislature without a vote and enjoys legislators' privileges. He parallels the Attorney General of India (Article 76).
concepts.example: A Minister of State with independent charge attends Cabinet only for his own matters.

questions.q: The Legislative Assembly of a State passes a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers. Which one of the following follows?
questions.a: The entire Council of Ministers must resign, including Ministers who are members of the Legislative Council
o: The entire Council of Ministers must resign, including Ministers who are members of the Legislative Council
Only the Cabinet Ministers must resign, while Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers continue until the Governor dismisses them
Only the Chief Minister must resign, since he alone is answerable to the Assembly for the Government's acts
Ministers who sit in the Legislative Council need not resign, since they are not answerable to the Assembly
questions.e: Collective responsibility to the Assembly means that on a no-confidence motion all the Ministers have to resign, including those who are members of the Legislative Council.
w: The whole Council falls; Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers do not stay on.
Responsibility is collective, so the whole Council resigns, not the Chief Minister alone.
Ministers from the Council are also bound by collective responsibility to the Assembly.

questions.q: Which one of the following describes the qualification of a person to be appointed Advocate-General of a State?
questions.a: Qualified to be a High Court Judge, that is, ten years as a High Court advocate or ten years in judicial service
o: Qualified to be a High Court Judge, that is, ten years as a High Court advocate or ten years in judicial service
Qualified to be a High Court Judge, that is, five years as a High Court advocate or five years in judicial service
An eminent jurist in the opinion of the Governor, even without practice at the Bar
Qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge, that is, ten years as an advocate of the Supreme Court
questions.e: The Advocate-General must be qualified for appointment as a High Court Judge: citizen of India with ten years in judicial office or as an advocate of a High Court.
w: The period is ten years, not five.
The Constitution makes no provision for appointing an eminent jurist as a High Court Judge, and the Advocate-General must be qualified as one.
That is the qualification for the Attorney General of India.

questions.q: Who appoints the Advocate-General of a State, and for what period does he hold office?
questions.a: The Governor appoints him, and he holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not for a fixed term
o: The Governor appoints him, and he holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not for a fixed term
The President appoints him on the advice of the Governor, and he holds office for a fixed term of five years
The Governor appoints him, and he holds office for a fixed term of five years like the Governor himself
The Chief Minister appoints him, and he holds office for as long as the Chief Minister chooses

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Reserving a Bill for the President, recommending President's Rule and appointing a Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority are key discretionary powers. Statement 2 is correct: Article 159; the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the State High Court, or the senior-most available Judge in his absence. Statement 3 is incorrect: That was the 7th Amendment of 1956. Statement 4 is incorrect: The five-year term is subject to the pleasure of the President, who may remove him at any time. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

Statement 4 is incorrect: the Assembly members from Tuensang are elected by the Regional Council, not directly by the people. So exactly 3 statements are correct.

'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct (1, 2 and 3).
